diagram.caption: The response gate protects cache replacement, not immediate reads: the UI can continue reading an older snapshot.

steps.title: Separate current intent from cached data
steps.description: The heads map controls response acceptance; the snapshots map independently serves immediate UI reads.

steps.title: A response arrives after the head changes
steps.description: A load captured A, but the current head is B, so refresh returns without replacing the cached snapshot.

steps.title: A response matches the current head
steps.description: A load captured B and the current head remains B, so its snapshot replaces the cached value.

title: Keep stale writes from overwriting a document
summary: Generated by the real explanation writer from synthetic code

diagram.source:
shape: sequence_diagram
client: Client
handler: updateDocument
database: Database
client -> handler.run: "Save body with displayed version"
handler.run -> database: "UPDATE WHERE id and version match; increment version"
database -> handler.run: "rowsAffected: 0 or matching row count"
handler.run -> client: "0 → 409, otherwise → 200"
diagram.caption: The displayed version remains the write precondition; checking and updating happen in one database statement.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: The client supplies its displayed version, and the database decides whether that version still matches.
steps.change: Follow one save from the client through the conditional write and response.

steps.title: Keep the caller's version
steps.description: The precondition comes from the document the client displayed, not a fresh server read that could hide a stale edit.
steps.change: The client submits the edited body with expectedVersion.

steps.title: Check and write together
steps.description: There is no separate read-then-write gap: the database changes the body and increments the version only where both predicates match.
steps.change: One UPDATE applies the version precondition and mutation.

steps.title: Expose the conflict
steps.description: Zero affected rows becomes 409 rather than an automatic retry with a newer version; the caller must reload.
steps.change: The handler converts the affected-row count into the response status.

title: Bound batches without starving work
summary: Generated by the real explanation writer from synthetic code

diagram.source:
direction: right
pending: "Pending: [8, 5, 3]"
batch: "Batch: []\nWeight: 0 / 12"
decision: "Empty batch: admit head"
pending -> decision: "Inspect head only"
decision -> batch: "Admission decision"
scenarios: {
  admit: {
    pending.label: "Pending: [5, 3]"
    batch.label: "Batch: [8]\nWeight: 8 / 12"
    decision.label: "8 admitted; inspect 5 next"
    (decision -> batch)[0].style.stroke-width: 4
  }
  stop: {
    pending.label: "Pending: [5, 3]"
    batch.label: "Return: [8]\nWeight: 8 / 12"
    decision.label: "8 + 5 > 12: stop"
    decision.style.stroke-width: 4
    decision.tooltip: "Although 3 would fit, the function cannot reach it without skipping 5. The rejected head remains pending."
    (decision -> batch)[0].label: "Return without shifting 5"
  }
  overweight: {
    pending.label: "Pending: [2]"
    batch.label: "Return: [15]\nWeight: 15 / 12"
    decision.label: "15 admitted into empty batch\n15 + 2 > 12: stop"
    decision.style.stroke-width: 4
    decision.tooltip: "The overflow guard requires a nonempty batch. This lets the first overweight item run, but prevents adding the next positive-weight item."
    (decision -> batch)[0].label: "Progress exception, then stop"
  }
}
diagram.caption: The batch is an ordered prefix, not a best-fit selection; its first item may exceed the limit.

steps.title: Start with an empty batch
steps.description: For [8,5,3] and limit 12, only the queue head is considered; an empty batch permits admission.

steps.title: Admit 8
steps.description: Shifting 8 leaves 5 at the head and sets the accumulated weight to 8.

steps.title: Stop rather than skip
steps.description: Adding 5 would exceed 12, so the function returns [8] without considering the later 3.

steps.title: An oversized head still progresses
steps.description: For the independent input [15,2], the empty-batch exception admits 15; the next comparison stops the batch and leaves 2 pending.
